title_en: Brookfield’s Connor Teskey on the Real Bottleneck in the AI Buildout
title_zh: Brookfield 的 Connor Teskey：AI 建设真正的瓶颈
subtitle_zh: Brookfield CEO Connor Teskey：AI 基建不缺资本不缺需求，缺的是把项目落地的运营能力。
description: Brookfield’s Connor Teskey on the Real Bottleneck in the AI Buildout

turns.en: Demand has become the critical input to growth for every major company in every major country around the world and there is a scarcity of it. The growth we're seeing across critical infrastructure assets and the overwhelming need for energy around the world goes so far beyond simply artificial intelligence.
turns.zh: 需求已经成为全球每一个主要国家、每一家大型公司增长的关键投入要素，而且它是稀缺的。我们在关键基础设施资产上看到的增长，以及全球对能源的压倒性需求，远远超出人工智能本身。

turns.en: Demand is up here and supply is down here. Even if demand growth was to slow, even if it was to plateau, even if it was to decline, there would still be a huge supply demand imbalance to the providers. It is perhaps the greatest capital need in the history of mankind. It's pretty exciting.
turns.zh: 需求在上头，供给在下头。即便需求增长放缓，即便见顶，甚至回落，对供应商而言依然存在巨大的供需失衡。这也许是人类历史上最大的资本需求。想想就令人振奋。

turns.en: Welcome to Goldman Sachs Exchange's Great Investors. I'm Allison Mas. Today I'm sitting down with Connor Teske, CEO of Brookfield Asset Management. Connor joined Brookfield in 2012 at age 24. 14 years later he runs the entire asset management business managing approximately $1.3 trillion across infrastructure, renewable power, real estate, private equity, and credit while continuing to lead its energy group. In this episode we discuss Connor's
turns.zh: 欢迎来到 Goldman Sachs Exchanges 的 Great Investors 系列，我是 Allison Moss。今天和我对坐的是 Brookfield Asset Management 的 CEO Connor Teskey。Connor 2012 年、24 岁时加入 Brookfield，14 年后，他执掌整个资产管理业务，管理着约 1.3 万亿美元资产，横跨基础设施、可再生能源、房地产、私募股权和信贷，同时继续领导其能源业务。在本期节目里，我们讨论了 Connor 的

turns.en: transition to the CEO seat, Brookfield's AI infrastructure build-out across the US and Europe, and the firm's strategic expansion and credit.
turns.zh: 接任 CEO 席位这一过渡、Brookfield 在美国和欧洲的 AI 基础设施扩建，以及公司向信贷领域的战略扩张。

turns.en: Connor, welcome to Great Investors. It's so fantastic to have you here. Thank you for having us. So across all those asset classes that you play in, is there one that you're most excited about right now? I'm probably a little bit biased. I have spent the last 10 years as part of the energy team, a business that's grown very very rapidly. I still lead that business today. I think if there was one theme across Brookfield that is quite dominant right now, it's
turns.zh: Connor，欢迎来到 Great Investors，真的太高兴你能来了。——谢谢你请我们来。——那么在你覆盖的所有这些资产类别里，你现在最兴奋的是哪一个？——我可能有点偏心眼。过去十年我一直待在能源团队，那项业务增长得非常非常快，直到今天我仍然领导着它。我想，如果说 Brookfield 眼下有一个相当主导的主题，那就是

turns.en: energy and infrastructure. A lot of the growth in that space, a portion of it is undoubtedly being driven by AI, and AI infrastructure is a huge theme at Brookfield, but the growth we're seeing across critical infrastructure assets and the overwhelming need for energy around the world goes so far beyond simply artificial intelligence, and that is one that the capital needs are bigger than at any point in history. It is perhaps the greatest capital need in
turns.zh: 能源和基础设施。这块的增长，毫无疑问有一部分是 AI 驱动的，AI 基础设施在 Brookfield 是一个大主题，但我们在关键基础设施资产上看到的增长、全球对能源的压倒性需求，远超人工智能本身，而且恰恰是在这里，资本需求比历史上任何时候都大。这也许是人类历史上最大的资本

turns.en: the history of mankind, and the returns are very attractive, and we see this this theme not enduring for quarters or years, but through the end of this decade and beyond. It's pretty exciting. It must be really fun for the energy team investors to have you sitting at the table. Yes, and energy is just a fun place to play right now. In only four or five years, electricity is something that everyone took for granted, and now all of a sudden it is the
turns.zh: 需求，而且回报率非常诱人。我们看到这个主题不会只持续几个季度或几年，而是贯穿到这个十年末并延续下去。想想就令人兴奋。——能源团队的投资者有你坐在桌上，一定很开心吧？——是的，能源现在就是一个很好玩的地方。仅仅四五年前，电力还是大家习以为常的东西，而现在它突然成了

turns.en: single bit of biggest bottleneck to growth for the greatest companies around the world and the largest countries around the world, and being a provider of that is an exciting place to be. So let's continue on the theme of AI, which you brought up. What is your read on the build out? If there was one headline or narrative that we hear a lot in the market that is detached from what we're seeing in the fundamentals on the ground, it's that the demand for AI
turns.zh: 全球最大公司、最大国家增长的单一最大瓶颈，而作为它的提供者，是一个非常令人兴奋的位置。——那我们接着聊你提到的 AI 这个话题。你怎么看这轮建设扩张？——如果说市场上有一个标题或叙事，与我们在实地看到的基本面是脱节的，那就是：对 AI

turns.en: infrastructure and the demand for the energy that supports it is in some way fragile. You know, we've seen the market react quite heavily to certain announcements. Oh, a potentially more efficient model comes out, or a large hyperscale scaler walks away from one of its multiple thousands of data center leases, and the whole market reacts. That seems a little divorced from what we're seeing on the ground. Right now, demand is exceptionally high and
turns.zh: 基础设施的需求、以及对支撑它的能源的需求，在某种程度上是脆弱的。你看，市场对某些公告反应很大——哦，出了一个可能更高效的模型，或者某个超大规模云厂商（hyperscaler）退掉了它数千份数据中心租约中的一份，整个市场就剧烈反应。这似乎与我们在实地看到的有点脱节。眼下，需求高得异常，

turns.en: supply is only a small fraction of that demand. Demand is up here and supply is up down here. Therefore, even if demand growth was to slow, even if it was to plateau, even if it was to decline, there would still be a huge supply demand imbalance to the providers of those assets and those inputs into that ecosystem. So obviously, a huge amount of discipline is required. These are huge projects. It's a large sum of capital that's going to go into the ground for
turns.zh: 而供给只是那部分需求的一小角。需求在上头，供给在下头。所以即便需求增长放缓，即便见顶，甚至回落，对这些资产的提供者、对那个生态系统投入品的供应商来说，仍然存在巨大的供需失衡。所以显然，需要极高的纪律。这些都是巨型项目，是一笔庞大的资本，要埋进地里

turns.en: multiple decades going forward, but the demand is absolutely overwhelming and not that imbalance is not going to be disturbed by small changes. The other thing that we're seeing on the AI side is so much talk goes to the big numbers because the numbers are quite frankly... Staggering. Staggering. Thank you. That is not the bottleneck. There is no shortage of capital and there is no shortage of demand. The bottleneck is who can actually pull these projects out of the
turns.zh: 未来好几十年，但需求是压倒性的，那种失衡不会被小变化扰乱。我们在 AI 侧看到的另一件事是，太多讨论都聚焦在那些大数字上，因为那些数字坦白讲……——惊人。——惊人，谢谢。但那不是瓶颈。资本不缺，需求也不缺。真正的瓶颈是谁能真正把项目从地里

turns.en: ground, who has the capabilities to complete the land development, secure the grid connection, build the power supply, build and operate a large scale gigafactory, provide the redundancy. That is the scarce input. It is not capital. It is not demand and we are increasingly seeing the market flow to not just simply those that can show up with big dollars, but those that can show up with both big dollars and big operating capabilities as well. Alright, so you've already built
turns.zh: 拔出来，谁有能力完成土地开发、拿下电网接入、建好电力供应、建造并运营超大规模的千兆工厂（gigafactory）、提供冗余备份。那才是稀缺的投入要素。不是资本，也不是需求。我们越来越看到，市场流向的不只是能带着大钱出现的人，而是能同时带着大钱和大运营能力出现的人。——好，你已经在（美国）建成了

turns.en: significant AI infrastructure in the US and now you're taking that push into Europe. So what is driving that expansion and what do you think travels across the Atlantic well and what doesn't? So both are going to see very significant build-outs, but the origins of those build-outs and the demand factors are going to be a little bit different. We can have a thoughtful debate, but of the 15 greatest technology companies in the world, the vast
turns.zh: 相当规模的 AI 基础设施，现在正向欧洲推进。是什么在驱动这轮扩张？你觉得哪些东西能跨过大西洋、哪些过不去？——两边都会看到非常大规模的建设，但建设的起点和需求因素会有些不同。我们可以好好辩一辩，但全球最好的十五家科技公司里，绝大多

turns.en: majority of them are based here in the United States and those corporates are driving a ton of corporate demand and an organic build-out of the AI infrastructure in this country and that's really being driven by the large technology companies, the hyperscalers and all of society in the United States is going to benefit from that. What's interesting is Europe doesn't have that same concentration of homegrown large-scale technology companies that
turns.zh: 数都扎在美国这里，这些企业正在驱动大量的企业需求，也在推动这个国家 AI 基础设施的有机建设，而这真的是由大型科技公司、超大规模云厂商们在驱动，美国全社会都会从中受益。有意思的是，欧洲没有那种本土大型科技公司的集中度，可以提供

turns.en: can provide that corporate demand. That doesn't mean we're not seeing significant growth, but it's coming from two different places. One, the large global technology companies, yes most of them are American, but they are global, so they are of course expanding into Europe as well, but the other demand driver that we think is underappreciated is we're actually seeing sovereign step-in in places where that corporate demand is not going to be the catalyst for the AI
turns.zh: 那种企业需求。这并不意味着我们没看到显著增长，但增长来自两个不同的地方。一是大型全球科技公司——没错，大部分是美国公司，但它们是全球化的，所以当然也在向欧洲扩张。另一个我们认为被低估的需求驱动，是我们实际上正看到主权力量下场，去填补那些企业需求无法成为 AI

turns.en: build-out. We're seeing the nation-states, what is AI? At its core it's a productivity tool. It's designed to drive efficiency and enable more growth.
turns.zh: 建设催化剂的地方。我们看到民族国家在……AI 是什么？本质上它是一个生产力工具，设计出来就是为了驱动效率、带来更多增长。

turns.en: We're seeing nation-states step in and say we don't want our population, our country to be left behind in having access to those tools and those productivity gains in the future, so they will actually backstop the build-out of AI infrastructure. We've signed agreements in France, in Sweden, in Qatar where the initial off-taker to support the build-out of AI infrastructure is not a hyperscaler, but actually a sovereign. We call that sovereign AI. We see
turns.zh: 我们看到民族国家下场说，我们不想让自己的人口、自己的国家在未来错失这些工具、错失这些生产力收益，所以它们实际上会给 AI 基础设施的建设兜底。我们已经在法国、瑞典、卡塔尔签了协议，那里支持 AI 基础设施建设的首个承购方（off-taker）不是超大规模云厂商，而是主权主体。我们把它叫作主权 AI（sovereign AI）。我们看到

turns.en: that demand much more in places outside of the United States and or Asia pack where you do have those domestic global technology leaders. That's an interesting perspective, sovereign AI. So the power side of this isn't new territory for you as you've talked about, it's where you started. You built most of the renewables business that's been long-core to Brookfield, but the argument has changed. It used to be a climate case and now it sounds like more
turns.zh: 那种需求更多出现在美国或亚太之外的地方——那些地方你没有本土的全球科技龙头。——这是个很有意思的视角，主权 AI。那么这件事的电力侧对你来说并不是新领域，你自己也说过，那是你的起点。你一手打造了长期作为 Brookfield 核心的可再生能源业务的大部分，但论点变了。过去它是气候叙事，现在听起来更多是

turns.en: of a commercial one. Speed to market, availability, energy, security. So has the thesis changed in your view or has the customer changed? What has changed? A lot has changed in the last five to ten years, but the one thing I would say about our approach that's been quite helpful and in this existed long before my time is our approach has always been driven by commercial. We don't take technology bats. We don't ever accept one basis point of return discount
turns.zh: 商业叙事——入市速度、可得性、能源安全。所以在你看来，是论点变了，还是客户变了？到底什么变了？——过去五到十年变了很多，但关于我们的方法，我想说的一点是它一直很有用，而且这在我来之前就存在了：我们的方法始终由商业驱动。我们不做技术押注，我们也从来不肯接受哪怕一个基点（bps）的回报折让

turns.en: because of the decarbonization or energy transition impact of an investment. We think you can make very attractive risk adjusted returns that also provide those benefits to society. What has changed is demand has become the critical input to growth for every major company in every major country around the world and there is a scarcity of it. There is a supply demand imbalance that started at the end of the last decade, the late 20 teens. Interestingly, at that
turns.zh: ，仅仅因为一项投资带有脱碳或能源转型的效应。我们认为你能做出非常有吸引力的风险调整后回报，同时为社会提供那些好处。变化在于，需求已经成为全球每一个主要国家、每一家大型公司增长的关键投入要素，而且它是稀缺的。这种供需失衡始于上一个十年末，也就是 2010 年代后期。有意思的是，在那个时点，

turns.en: point, it wasn't driven by AI. It was driven by these global trends of reindustrialization and electrification. That created a supply demand imbalance that in and of itself was going to exist for decades and provide multiple decades of electricity demand growth and then AI took off and took that supply demand imbalance and exaggerated it even further. We would say that we're seeing in our business is two things. Electrons are a
turns.zh: 它并不是由 AI 驱动的，而是由再工业化和电气化这些全球趋势驱动的。那制造了一个供需失衡，它本身就将存在几十年，并提供几十年的电力需求增长；然后 AI 起飞了，把这个供需失衡进一步放大了。我们在自己业务里看到的，我认为是两件事。电子（electrons）是一种大宗商品，

turns.en: commodity, but there is a lot more sophistication around electrons now. Counter parties don't just phone up and say they want power. They want power that's a certain shape in a certain location from a certain source for a certain duration. Being able to evolve and meet those ever-evolving customer needs is very, very critical to us. That's leading to the development of new technologies. I'll tell you the fastest growing segment of our energy business
turns.zh: 但现在围绕电力的讲究多多了。交易对手不再只是打电话来说他们要电。他们要的电力是特定形态、在特定位置、来自特定电源、持续特定时长的。能够演进、满足这些不断演化的客户需求，对我们非常非常关键。这正在催生新技术的开发。我可以告诉你，我们能源业务眼下增长最快的板块

turns.en: right now is energy storage. How do you get the joys of low-cost renewables but offset the issues of intermittency? You offset it with energy storage and batteries, which is undoubtedly the fastest. That wasn't true five years ago.
turns.zh: 就是储能。怎么在享受低成本可再生能源的好处的同时，抵消间歇性的问题？用储能和电池来抵消，这无疑是增长最快的。五年前可不是这样。

turns.en: The other thing that we are seeing is because electricity has become such a critical bottleneck, the largest buyers and users of electricity around the world don't always just go to who can provide it at the lowest cost. It is very negative for a hyperscaler if they want to turn on a data center but the power supply isn't available yet. Rather than having 10,000 small suppliers who may or may not get a project delivered on time or on budget, we're increasingly seeing
turns.zh: 我们看到的另一件事是，因为电力已经变成如此关键的瓶颈，全球最大的电力买家和用户，并不总是去找报价最低的人。对超大规模云厂商来说，想打开一个数据中心、但电力供应还没到位，是非常负面的。与其要一万个可能按时、按预算交付、也可能做不到的小供应商，我们越来越看到

turns.en: the largest users of electricity increasingly focus on a smaller number of scale providers who have the credibility to work through problems, deliver on time, deliver on budget, and really can be a partner to them in providing what is one of the most critical inputs. Our business over the last five or ten years, ten years ago, we essentially sold power to utilities and governments. Today we sell the
turns.zh: 最大的电力使用者越来越聚焦到更少数的规模化供应商身上——他们有能力解决问题、按时交付、按预算交付，真正能成为他们的伙伴，去提供这一最关键的投入要素。我们的业务在过去五到十年里：十年前，我们基本上把电卖给公用事业公司和政府；今天，我们把

turns.en: most majority of our power directly to corporates and we work very much with those corporates to meet their evolving needs and our relationships with them go beyond individual contracts to global scale framework agreements that just continue to grow and grow over time. That makes sense. Certainty and ability to deliver. It's far more value than picking up a penny here or a penny there on power price. So everything that you've described gets built with borrowed money
turns.zh: 绝大部分电力直接卖给企业，我们和这些企业紧密合作，去满足他们不断演化的需求；我们与他们的关系超越了单个合同，升级为全球规模的框架协议，并且随时间不断壮大。——有道理，确定性和交付能力。这比在电价上捡一美分、那美分要有价值得多。所以你描述的这一切，都是靠借来的钱建造的，

turns.en: which brings me to credit and in your story there's a mix of organic and inorganic. You've built a lot in-house but you've also bought a majority stake in Oak Tree, Howard Marx's firm back in 2019, and now full ownership plus stakes in several other managers. So how do you decide what you're going to build versus what you're going to buy? The build versus buy decision is one that we make every time we look to grow at Brookfield. It is always a build versus buy
turns.zh: 这就把话题引到了信贷上。在你的故事里，有机的和外延的兼而有之。你们自建了很多，但你们在 2019 年买下了 Oaktree——Howard Marks 的公司——的多数股权，如今是全仓控股，再加上对其他几家管理公司的持股。那么，你们怎么决定什么要自建、什么要收购？——自建还是收购，这个 build versus buy 的决定，是我们在 Brookfield 每次寻求增长时都要做的。它永远是一道

turns.en: decision and in general we prefer to build it ourselves if we think we have the capabilities to do so because it's often less expensive and two you can build it exactly how you want it. Sam Pollock who's built our infrastructure business over the last 20 years he's built an incredible market leading franchise. It does not have a peer. If he wants to launch a new strategy he's not going to go buy someone else to do it. He's very likely going to use some
turns.zh: 自建还是收购的选择题。大体上，如果我们认为自己有能力，我们更倾向于自己建，因为那样通常更便宜，而且第二，你可以完全按你想要的样子来建。Sam Pollock 在过去二十年里打造了我们的基础设施业务，建起了一个了不起的、市场领先的业务板块，它没有对手。如果他想发起一个新策略，他不会去买别人来做。他很可能会动用一些

turns.en: internal resources to build the strategy from the ground up. However from time to time we see capabilities that we think it would be very difficult to replicate or it would take us too long to replicate in order to capture what we think is a very large and attractive market opportunity and that that was exactly Oak Tree for us in 2019. We had a very large and market leading equity franchise on the private investment side but we did feel that credit was
turns.zh: 内部资源，把策略从头建起来。但有时候，我们会看到一些能力，我们认为很难复制，或者复制起来要花我们太长时间，而为了抓住我们认为非常大、非常有吸引力的市场机会，那就值得出手——2019 年对我们来说那正是 Oaktree。我们在私募投资侧已经有一个非常大、市场领先的股权业务，但我们确实感到，信贷正在

turns.en: becoming a core pillar of private markets going forward and could we have built a market leading credit franchise over you know 10 or 15 years? Absolutely but we thought it was worth it to to accelerate that process and in hindsight we think it was a great decision and we couldn't be more thrilled with the the partnership with Oak Tree. So staying on Oak Tree for a second how did that deal start and how did you end up at the center of it? Like a lot of things
turns.zh: 变成未来私募市场（private markets）的一个核心支柱。我们能不能花十或十五年建出一个市场领先的信贷板块？当然能，但我们觉得值得加速那个过程。事后来看，我们认为那是个了不起的决定，我们对与 Oaktree 的合作不能再满意。——那我们在 Oaktree 上再多停一下：那笔交易当初是怎么开始的，你又是怎么站到它正中间的？

turns.en: some some good fortune. I actually started in the private equity group at Brookfield when I joined when I joined the firm in in Toronto almost 15 years ago. One of the first things I was asked to review was actually an investment in another asset manager that was in need for capital and I didn't really know where to start. I'd never looked at an asset management business before and after spinning my wheels for probably a few days I had this idea which was well
turns.zh: 和很多事情一样，有几分运气。其实我快十五年前在多伦多加入公司时，就是从私募股权团队起步的。我被要求评估的第一批事情之一，正好是对另一家需要资本的资产管理公司的投资。我真的不知道从哪里入手，我以前从来没看过一个资产管理业务。原地打转了大概几天之后，我冒出一个想法：嗯，如果

turns.en: if I can understand Brookfield's business model I can probably use that as a base case to try and understand that this other asset managers model and from that initial review we began as part of that process we simply began to track some of the other publicly traded alternative asset managers largely to see how Brookfield could be doing better and how were we doing versus our peer set and at the beginning of 2018 we felt that Oak Tree was not trading
